title: box_scramble round input
description: Evaluation shape for one round. Unlike upstream Humanoid Parkour (static, public geometry), the box field ITSELF is drawn from `seed` inside the referee (env/course.sample_boxes) -- fixed box count and zone roles (100 scramble / 60 push / 36 climb), sampled size/density/placement. Each instance's wind is drawn from the same seed (env/sim.instance_spec), so the suite differs every round and the box field is identical across every instance within one round.

seed.description: Round seed: the whole box field (sizes, densities, placement) AND every instance's wind derive from it. One draw per round, fresh each round, so every instance in a round faces the identical field and the field rotates between rounds. Required rather than optional on purpose: a missing seed would silently freeze the box field instead of failing.

num_instances.description: Evaluation instances. Every instance in a round shares the identical box field; only wind varies between them, so this sets how well the suite covers the wind range, not how many box fields are sampled. MEASURED 2026-09-08 in a PR environment (apex-mvp#452): the inherited 24 does NOT fit. A control step costs ~29 ms under concurrency, so 24 instances share 780 s at ~32.5 s each = ~1100 steps, and 43.7% of instances ended `time_limit`. 12 x 2000 costs ~700 s and fits with headroom; 8 instances is the most that can reach a full 3000 steps. Cutting instances is cheap here because they share one box field, so round variance is dominated by that single draw and does not fall as sqrt(N).

max_steps_per_episode.description: Control-step cap per instance (1 step = 20 ms sim time, so 2000 = 40 s). MEASURED 2026-09-08 (apex-mvp#452): the inherited 3000 is unreachable in practice -- at ~29 ms per control step under concurrency, 24 instances sharing a 780 s budget get ~1100 steps each, so the cap advertised was never the cap applied. Either keep this at/below what `time_budget_s / num_instances` actually buys, or cut num_instances. The referee's time budget is what really bounds the suite; this bounds one instance's simulated length.

deadline_ms.description: Per-/act deadline for the policy, enforced by the referee's HTTP client. Unchanged from upstream.

wind_max_ms.description: Upper bound of the per-instance wind draw, in m/s; speed is uniform on [0, this] and direction is uniform over the full circle. Default 8.0 (env/sim.WIND_MAX_MS) is Beaufort 4 at the robot, worth 3.6% of body weight in drag -- unchanged from upstream parkour. 0 disables wind. Tunable without a release, but it moves baseline_raw_score.

record_history.description: Write one replayable history file per instance to /data/history/, delivered to the miner as FileType.HISTORY. Optional and default-on; a write failure never affects the score.

history_stride.description: Keep every Nth control step in the history. Default 2 (25 Hz) via env/history.DEFAULT_STRIDE.

time_budget_s.description: Wall-clock seconds the whole instance suite may take, shared across the instances still to run (each gets `remaining / instances left`, so slack flows forward). An instance that reaches its share ends `time_limit` and is scored on the progress it made -- changed 2026-09-08, because zeroing it let contention decide the score and penalised the runs that lasted longest. Instances the budget never reached still score 0.0: no progress. Must sit comfortably below `referee.timeout_s` (900) in spec.yaml, which is a hard kill with no grace and no result. Leave real headroom: at 780 s, 3 of 50 load-test submissions still hit the kill and returned `referee_error`, because sandbox start and image pull are outside this budget but inside that timeout. Default 780 (env referee DEFAULT_SUITE_BUDGET_S); 700 is the measured-safe value for a 12 x 2000 round.
